clue.text: People going for promotion gather round head of department

indicators.note: round means the word for gather goes around the other piece

parts.note: to gather is to amass

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of department

explanation.surface: Staff seeking advancement crowd around their departmental boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' here is advertising, not a better job: the definition means the public at large targeted by ads.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass public that advertising targets is called by this coined term for consumers swayed by promotions.

clue.text: A custom briefly binding China to US state

indicators.note: binding means the first pieces wrap round the China word
briefly means the custom word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a habit is a custom
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate); an American would say bud

explanation.surface: A habit, briefly, ties China to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: BUD goes between A and HABI. 'China' is British rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the emirates making up the UAE, so it is a constituent state.

clue.text: Middlesex's opener with duck after a Lord's dismissal — one caught here?

indicators.note: the opener of Middlesex is its first letter, a cricket-flavoured way to signal the initial

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: dismissal means the a and Lord pieces are sent away from the duck word

parts.note: Donald Duck is the famous cartoon duck
LD is the abbreviation for Lord

explanation.surface: A Middlesex batsman makes a duck after being dismissed at Lord's, caught in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like a score of nought but is DONALD; removing A and LD (a Lord) leaves DON. Lord's is London's famous cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-on is a fielding position in cricket, a place where a fielder may take a catch.

clue.text: What's needed by florist looking up address for gentleman

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters are read from bottom to top
what's needed by points to letters held within the word florist

explanation.surface: A florist checks a directory for a gentleman's address.
explanation.walkthrough: RIS sits inside 'florist'; 'looking up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the polite form of address used to a man, or the title of a knight.

clue.text: Green light from molten rock containing gold pennies, reflecting

indicators.note: reflecting means the whole assembly is read backwards, as in a mirror
containing means the lava word holds the gold and pennies pieces inside it

parts.note: molten rock flowing from a volcano is lava
OR is the heraldic word for gold
P is the abbreviation for penny, so PP is pennies

explanation.surface: A permit is issued for something about volcanic rock studded with gold coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts ORPP inside LAVA after LAV, giving LAVORPPA; 'reflecting' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A green light is an idiom for permission to go ahead, the same thing as official consent.

clue.text: Don't have entirely standard urban location

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
a town is an urban place

explanation.surface: Someone lacks a fully standard city address.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning a share of something jointly with others means you possess only a portion, never the whole of it.

clue.text: Unfortunate soldiers in range of capture without resistance

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the capture word surrounds the resistance letter

parts.note: something within range of capture can be got, so it is gettable
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Sadly, troops come within reach of being taken without a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means outside: GETTABLE goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfortunate is to be lamented, the same as something to be sorry about.

clue.text: See a show-head down to the centre in N American city

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: the head of the word for show moves down into its middle

parts.note: to uncover is to reveal or show

explanation.surface: Someone sees a performance and then heads downtown in a Canadian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The U at the head of UNCOVER drops to the centre, giving NCOUVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major Canadian city in British Columbia, so it is a North American city.

clue.text: Poet and singer flying home

parts.note: the lark is a songbird famous for singing in flight
in means at home

explanation.surface: A poet and a singer fly home together.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was a twentieth-century English writer of verse, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: A bit of swimming in Scottish port no good for one

indicators.note: no good for one means the no-good letters replace the one letter

parts.note: Leith is the port of Edinburgh
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A swim in a Scottish harbour is no good for anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: NG replaces the I in LEITH.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pool, one stretch from end to end is a single unit of a swim session.

clue.text: Nude shot back to collect women's briefs

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or broken up, so the letters of Nude are rearranged
to collect means the word for back gathers another piece inside it

parts.note: the rear is the back
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A nude photo is taken from behind to gather the material for a women's fashion piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles NUDE into UNDE; 'to collect' puts W inside REAR to give RWEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are a style of knickers or pants, so they are an example of what is worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: I'll cut off ungrateful daughter, being doomed

indicators.note: cut off means the letters of I'll are removed from the daughter's name

parts.note: Goneril is one of King Lear's two ungrateful daughters in Shakespeare's play
I'll, without its apostrophe, gives the letters IL

explanation.surface: A father vows to disinherit his thankless daughter, who is now finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is Lear threatening Goneril. 'being doomed' is a noun phrase: a creature that is doomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doomed being is someone past saving, which is exactly the colloquial noun for a person who is done for.

clue.text: Passing fancy, very much a description of close relationship?

definitions.text: very much a description of close relationship?

parts.note: passing something across is handing it
to fancy someone is to love them

explanation.surface: A brief crush seems to describe a very intimate bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing fancy' reads as a fleeting crush, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties who are in very close, often collusive, association, like a fist inside its covering.

clue.text: Travel to Rio resolved to work with singers

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken down into parts and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for Rio to perform with a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Il Trovatore is Verdi's opera, and an opera is a musical work performed by singers.

clue.text: Material band recalled in book at intervals

indicators.note: recalled means the picked letters are called back, read in reverse order
at intervals means every other letter of in book is taken

explanation.surface: A fabric strap is mentioned again at several points in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'in book' give IBO, which 'recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the broad sash worn round a Japanese kimono, a band made of fabric.

clue.text: Get intoxicated, long after beer having run out

indicators.note: after means the long piece is placed after the beer piece
having run out means the run abbreviation is dropped from the beer word

parts.note: a brew is a beer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to get drunk once the beer has all gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' (with 'having run') removes R from BREW to leave BEW; 'after' puts ITCH behind it. 'Get' is a verb: to captivate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To intoxicate someone figuratively is to enchant or captivate them, the sense of casting a spell over them.

clue.text: WW1 bomb ace dead

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a whizz
dead as in dead on, exactly, the same as bang on

explanation.surface: A First World War bomb kills an ace pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead' is an adverb meaning exactly, as in 'dead on' or 'bang on'.
explanation.definitionFit: This was soldiers' slang for a small high-velocity shell in the First World War, named for the noise it made.

clue.text: Local church body embracing appeal to the West

indicators.note: embracing means the church body word holds another piece inside it

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: to the West in an across clue means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: IT is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A parish council holds out an appeal to Western audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the West' turns IT into TI, which sits inside NAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is someone who belongs to a place by birth, the same as an inhabitant born there.

clue.text: Criminal keeps moving safe

indicators.note: keeps means the criminal word holds the moving word inside it

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
astir means up and moving about

explanation.surface: A criminal keeps shifting a safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like a strongbox, but it is an adjective meaning secure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-iron guarantee is one that is certain and unbreakable, so it is completely secure.

clue.text: Bookish plays with nothing edited out that you'd put on to finish off

definitions.text: that you'd put on to finish off

indicators.note: plays signals that the letters of Bookish are put into a new order
edited out means the nothing letter is struck from the fodder before it is rearranged

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: A studious type plays a part with a passage removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an O from BOOKISH and rearrange the remaining BKISH plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: You put the kibosh on something to stop it, so the word names whatever you apply to finish a plan off.

clue.text: Poor person's shelter all but closed up

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a door pushed to is nearly closed, so to means all but closed

explanation.surface: A homeless person's refuge has almost been shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: A door that is 'to' is pushed nearly shut; 'up' turns TO into OT. The 's is a link: poor person is.
explanation.definitionFit: The contrast between those with wealth and those without names the needy as the ones lacking means.

clue.text: Country some distance from China with old secret police chief

parts.note: the li is a traditional Chinese unit of distance
Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD

explanation.surface: A nation lies far from China and had a former spy boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a nation in West Africa, so it is an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Pulse is fast, with sickness not coming to an end

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: not coming to an end means the sickness word loses its final letter

parts.note: being ill is sickness

explanation.surface: Fasting is a pulse, while illness never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' is not a heartbeat but an edible seed of a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, and the lentil is one of them.

clue.text: Draw in muscles on heavenly body

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles
an orb is a sphere, poetically a star or planet

explanation.surface: Someone sketches muscles on a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something up is to take it in, as a sponge takes in water.

clue.text: Composer with neither energy nor time for informal affairs

indicators.note: with neither ... nor means both of the named letters are taken out of the composer

parts.note: Georges Bizet composed the opera Carmen
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A composer works without energy or time for casual affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nor' joins the two letters removed from BIZET.
explanation.definitionFit: Biz is slang shortening of business, used casually for one's affairs or trade.

clue.text: In modern times, those in front make fast progress

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks dates in the modern era
the van is the vanguard, those at the front
to cement is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: Nowadays the leaders make quick headway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means firm, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement means moving forward or promotion, the same as making progress.

clue.text: Gain this when guard's heading off?

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the guard word is removed

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: Get in here once the sentinel has gone away?
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': guard has heading off. Gaining this is getting in once the sentry has left.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain admission is a set phrase for getting in, where admission means the right to go inside.

clue.text: Catching game in heart of poor region Down Under

indicators.note: catching means the outer letters hold the game word inside them
heart of picks out the middle letters of poor

parts.note: tag is a chasing game played by children

explanation.surface: A playground game is caught in the middle of a deprived area.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'poor' is OO; TAG goes between those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island, and Down Under means Australia or New Zealand.

clue.text: Catch champ close to despair in tense affair

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them
to champ is to bite or chew noisily

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of despair

explanation.surface: A winner is nabbed on the brink of hopelessness during a nervy match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a champion, but it is the verb to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: A very nervy contest is one that makes spectators chew their nails, hence the compound for it.

clue.text: Wrap last agenda item up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: AOB, any other business, is the final item on a meeting agenda

explanation.surface: Finish off the last item of the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' looks like 'finish', but 'Wrap' alone is the definition: a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A long feathery scarf is worn round the neck as a wrap.

clue.text: Almost all butter's 'fit for posh bread

indicators.note: fit for posh means the fit word takes the place of the posh letter
almost all means the last letter of butter is dropped

parts.note: the word butter is used as printed, with its possessive 's giving no letters
U stands for upper-class, hence posh
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: Nearly all the butter is suited to fancy bread.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTE (butter less R) has its U replaced by AGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long thin French loaf, so it is a kind of the staple food.

clue.text: American's sweet daughter's left leg in gully

indicators.note: daughter's left means the daughter letter has departed from the sweet

parts.note: candy is the American word for a sweet
D is the abbreviation for daughter
the on side is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: An American girl's candy is dropped and a leg is stuck in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a narrow ravine, and a canyon is a deep, larger version of the same feature.
